property_summary: Only the account passed as msg.sender (not an externally-originated tx origin) can successfully call newEmergencyOracle through C when C.jojoTeam is set to that account.

For any caller (fuzzed address) who is set as jojoTeam and who calls newEmergencyOracle, the newly deployed EmergencyOracle's owner should equal the caller (msg.sender); the mutant that constructs with address(this) makes the new oracle's owner equal the factory contract instead, breaking this rule for some inputs.

For any caller who is set as jojoTeam and invokes newEmergencyOracle(description), the created EmergencyOracle.owner() must equal the caller (msg.sender); the mutant that passes address(this) as owner makes the new oracle owner be the factory contract instead, violating this property for callers who are jojoTeam.

For any caller set as jojoTeam who calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the newly created EmergencyOracle's owner() must equal the caller (msg.sender); the mutant that uses address(this) as constructor owner makes the new oracle owned by the factory contract instead, breaking this rule for those calls.

For any jojoTeam caller who invokes newEmergencyOracle(description), the created EmergencyOracle's owner() must be the jojoTeam caller (the msg.sender); the mutant that passes address(this) to the EmergencyOracle constructor makes the new oracle owned by the factory contract instead, breaking this rule for those calls.

For any caller that is set as jojoTeam and calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the newly deployed EmergencyOracle's owner() equals the caller (msg.sender) in the reference; the mutant that constructs the oracle with address(this) makes the owner be the factory contract, violating this rule for some jojoTeam callers.

For any caller (jojoTeam) that creates a new EmergencyOracle via newEmergencyOracle, the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed parameter (owner) equals the caller address; the mutant emits the newOracle address instead, violating this rule for inputs where newOracle != caller.

For any caller address that is jojoTeam, when newEmergencyOracle(...) is called the emitted NewEmergencyOracle owner field equals the caller (msg.sender); the mutant emits newOracle instead, which differs whenever newOracle != msg.sender.

For any jojoTeam caller who calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed parameter (owner) equals the jojoTeam caller address; the mutant emits newOracle instead, which can differ when the new EmergencyOracle's address != caller.

For any jojoTeam caller, after calling newEmergencyOracle(description) the C contract's JojoTeam getter (jojoTeam) remains equal to the caller (the contract must not change who jojoTeam is); the mutant does not modify jojoTeam either, so we instead assert that the NewEmergencyOracle event's emitted owner equals the jojoTeam (caller) by capturing the emitted logs via a helper that forwards txs so the log owner differs when mutant emits newOracle — we detect mismatch by calling newEmergencyOracle via a helper contract that calls C as jojoTeam and then reading the emitted owner through the helper's returned lastOwner value (the reference returns caller as owner, the mutant returns newOracle), so the property is: after the helper invokes newEmergencyOracle, the helper-observed owner equals the helper address (caller); the mutant will sometimes return a different owner (the newly deployed EmergencyOracle) and fail this assertion.

When jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the NewEmergencyOracle event's first parameter (owner) equals the jojoTeam caller address for every admissible input; the mutant emits newOracle there instead, so for some inputs (where newOracle != caller) the mutant violates this rule.

After any successful call to newEmergencyOracle by the jojoTeam address, the contract's jojoTeam state must remain equal to the caller (i.e. jojoTeam does not change during creation); the mutant wrongly assigns jojoTeam = msg.sender inside the function which can change jojoTeam and thus violate this for some inputs.

For any caller X that is initially the jojoTeam, calling newEmergencyOracle(...) must NOT change the stored jojoTeam value (it should remain X); the mutant assigns jojoTeam = msg.sender inside the function which can overwrite jojoTeam and thus violates this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller who is the current jojoTeam, after calling newEmergencyOracle(description) the stored jojoTeam remains unchanged (the reference never mutates jojoTeam inside the call); the mutant assigns jojoTeam = msg.sender inside the function which can change jojoTeam and thus violates this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller A that is NOT the current jojoTeam, attempts to call newEmergencyOracle should revert (onlyJojoTeam); the mutant that assigns jojoTeam = msg.sender before creating the oracle can allow a non-jojoTeam caller to become jojoTeam only inside the call and so may change behavior — but the correct contract always reverts for non-jojoTeam callers, so the property is: newEmergencyOracle succeeds iff the caller equals c.jojoTeam() prior to the call.

After a successful call to newEmergencyOracle by the jojoTeam, the owner recorded inside the newly created EmergencyOracle (returned as the NewEmergencyOracle event's first argument / constructor param) must equal the jojoTeam at the moment BEFORE the call; the mutant writes jojoTeam = msg.sender before construction which can change jojoTeam prior to it being used as owner and so can cause the deployed EmergencyOracle.owner() to differ from the pre-call jojoTeam for some callers.
